text:
sam.engineer: Hey all - weird payment flow on DevSummit ticket. I bought the conference pass on the company card (CorpCard ****1234). Organizer emailed that the event got postponed and instead of issuing a refund they provided a $950 credit voucher valid 12 months. They say refunds are "rare" and will only issue cash if requested within 7 days.

alex.finance: Sorry for the headache. Short policy: our preference is refund to original payment method so the card charge clears. Credits/vouchers are acceptable only if Procurement approves using the credit for a future approved purchase. We avoid leaving employee or corporate cards with outstanding vendor credits for long periods because it complicates monthly close.

procurement-bot: procurement note: if vendor credit is accepted, procurement must create a PO or ticket to reserve the credit against a future invoice. Vendor credits should be documented with a credit memo that includes vendor name, amount, credit ID, and expiry date.

sam.engineer: I already booked travel that week too and those flight/hotel charges are separate. The ticket charge is still on the card. What happens during reconciliation if we keep the credit instead of refunding?

alex.finance: Two paths: 1) Refund to card: finance will request organizer refund within the 7-day window. Once refunded, the card charge will drop off and nothing else needed. 2) Accept voucher: Procurement signs off and finance records a vendor credit memo. At month-end we'll book a contra-charge (credit) against travel expense when the credit is applied. If we accepted credit but then never use it, we may need to expense it as a loss after the credit expires.

procurement-bot: For path 2, we need the vendor credit memo PDF, vendor terms, and an email thread showing credit ID and expiry. Also a manager approval indicating we'll use the credit for future DevSummit or an equivalent training budget.

sam.engineer: I used the CorpCard. If we accept the credit and it gets used later, does that reduce my future event approvals? I don't want to be stuck with admin overhead.

alex.finance: If the credit remains on the corporate vendor account and Procurement/Events kick off the next purchase, finance will apply the credit before charging the card. You won't be out of pocket. If we seek a refund to the card and the vendor refuses, finance will escalate.

nora.events: Events prefers refunds to the card when possible to avoid credit tracking. If vendor insists on credit, we'll take the credit for the team and mark it in our event budget tracker with the credit ID and expiry date. Also please forward the vendor email and the credit voucher.

receipts-bot: credit voucher uploaded: 2251234700_devsummit-credit-950.pdf

receipts-bot: original invoice uploaded: 2251234710_devsummit-invoice-950.pdf

sam.engineer: Thanks, uploaded both. One extra case: what if the ticket had been personally charged and I was reimbursed already? Then the vendor issues me (employee) a credit voucher. Can I keep it or do I need to return it to the company?

alex.finance: If a personal card was used and you were reimbursed by Redwood, the credit belongs to Redwood. Policy requires employees to surrender vendor credits that correspond to reimbursed expenses. There are two options: a) vendor re-issue the credit to corporate account, or b) employee applies credit to a future vendor purchase and remits equivalent cash to company (not preferred). Document the credit transfer and get manager signoff.

procurement-bot: Action items: 1) Sam: get explicit vendor language showing credit ID + expiry and confirm they can reassign credit to Redwood account (if not possible, request cash refund within 7 days). 2) Alex/Finance: attempt refund request now and track vendor response. 3) Nora/Events: hold tentative reservation for next DevSummit and mark credit in event budget if procurement approves.

sam.engineer: I'll email the vendor requesting refund to card or reassign credit to Redwood and drop the thread here. Thanks!
